Council Meeting Minutes for
City of Cabot, Arkansas
Cabot Justice Center
805 W. Main St.
Cabot, AR 72023
February 2, 2026
6:30 pm.

This event was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be
viewed here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PXvG5TJBjq4.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council
at 6:47 pm after a Work Session. Council Member Stephen Redd led the prayer,
and Council Member Matt Webber led the pledge of allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
James Reid, Stephen Redd, Maggie Cope, Kyle Pickard, Matt Webber, and
Brandon Hillenburg. Ed Long and Corey Spangle were absent. Others
present were Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, Deputy City
Attorney Courtnie Holt, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Reid, motioned to approve the minutes of the
January 12 meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Reid, motioned only to read the legislation by
title. The motion passed unanimously.

City Council Old Business

OLD BUSINESS: RESOLUTION NO. 15 OF 2025 - A RESOLUTION
AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING THE RETURN OF FUNDS TO THE CABOT
WATER AND WASTEWATER COMMISSION UNDER CERTAIN
CONDITIONS; AMENDING THE GENERAL FUND OF THE 2025 ANNUAL
OPERATING BUDGET; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by the City
Clerk/Treasurer by title only. Discussion followed. Mr. Hillenburg made a motion
to amend the legislation to take effect on April 1, 2026. The motion was
seconded by Mr. Redd and passed by roll call vote, 6-0. Mr. Redd then made a
motion to adopt the legislation as amended. The motion was seconded by Mr.
Hillenburg and passed by roll call vote, 6-0. Mayor Kincade stated that he
reserves the right to veto.

CONFIRMED NEW BUSINESS BY VOTE OF THE COUNCIL: Mr. Redd moved
to confirm Agenda Items (a) Resolution No. 5, (b) Resolution No. 6, and (c)
Resolution No. 7. The motion was seconded by Mr. Webber and passed
unanimously by roll-call vote.
--- page 6 (OCR) ---
RESOLUTION 5 OF 2026 — A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND
CITY CLERK-TREASURER TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH CTS
SERVICES, INC.; TO WAIVE THE COMPETITIVEBIDDING REQUIREMENTS IN
ORDER TO ENTER INTO SAID AGREEMENT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was
read by the City Clerk/Treasurer by title only. Mr. Redd made a motion to adopt.
The motion was seconded by Mr. Reid and passed by roll call vote, 6-0.

RESOLUTION 6 OF 2026 — A RESOLUTION APPROVING OF THE AWARD OF A
SERVICE WEAPON; AUTHORIZING THE SALE OF A DUTY SHOTGUN; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES was read by the City Clerk/Treasurer by title only. Mr. Reid
made a motion to adopt. The motion was seconded by Mr. Redd and passed by
roll call vote, 6-0.

RESOLUTION 7 OF 2026 - A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY
CLERK-TREASURER TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH HALFF ASSOCIATES
FOR THE RODNEY GUTHRIE DRAINAGE STUDY PROJECT; AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES was read by the City Clerk/Treasurer by title only. Mr. Hillenburg
made a motion to adopt. The motion was seconded by Mr. Webber and passed
by roll call vote, 6-0.

Community Input: A citizen requested that the City explore the possibility of
an on-call public transit system to assist low-income residents and to determine
whether such a program could be supported through grant funding. Mayor
Kincade stated that he would look into the matter. The citizen noted that
Arkadelphia operates a city-funded on-call transit system.

Mayoral Input:

Council Member Input.

Adjournment: The meeting adjourned at 7:19 pm.

ORDINANCE NO. 9 OF 2026

AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING ADDITIONAL INSPECTION RELATED
REQUIREMENTS FOR CITY OWNED PROPERTIES IN CERTAIN
SITUATIONS; AND OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot owns buildings within city limits, and multiple of said
buildings are subject to lease agreements and/or have been recently remodeled; and

WHEREAS, while the city employs building and code inspectors, the Cabot City Council
believes that city owned buildings would benefit from additional inspections performed by state
inspectors in certain circumstances; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council hereby sets forth the circumstances on when
additional inspections from state inspectors are required.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the City Council of the City of Cabot,
Arkansas that:

SECTION 1: The City must pass state level inspection(s) from any applicable state
office when a City-owned building is constructed, remodeled, or leased. Applicable City-owned
buildings that do not pass said inspection(s) may not be utilized by the City or leased to a third
party. The City must request and work in good faith to accomplish any inspection(s) required by
this Ordinance.

SECTION 2: For purposes of this Ordinance, “remodeled” refers to any construction on
or refurbishment of a City-owned building after the effective date of this Ordinance that would
require a permit under City code.

SECTION 3: For purposes of this Ordinance, “leased” buildings refer to buildings
subject to lease agreements that are executed after the effective date of this Ordinance. This
Ordinance shall not be interpreted to impose new conditions on currently enacted lease
agreements or to improperly interfere with currently enacted lease agreements.

SECTION 4: The Cabot City Council recognizes that nether it nor the City have direct
authority over state inspectors and do not have ability to mandate that state inspectors perform
the requested inspections. As such, the City shall not be in violation of this Ordinance if it
requests an inspection required herein and a representative of the applicable state office declines
the request or otherwise fails to perform the required inspection.

SECTION 5: In addition to the other requirements of this Ordinance, the City must
comply with all city ordinances, city code sections, and UDC provisions when constructing or
remodeling city-owned buildings. Additionally, the City must seek and receive Cabot Planning
Commission approval for all items required by city ordinances, city code sections, and UDC
provision when constructing or remodeling city-owned buildings.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION – Old 67/1st Street Drainage
The Engineer will provide all professional services necessary to perform a flood hazard study of
the Drain 2 in the vicinity of Old Highway 67 and contributing areas. The study area follows an
open channel from the culvert crossing at the Union Pacific Railroad near the end of South
Adams Street to the vicinity of South 6th Street. The study includes tributary areas to this
channel. The study is more particularly defined by Tasks 1 and 2 (Data Collection and Survey &
Existing Conditions Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modeling), and final deliverable includes a report
with recommendations for future capital improvements.

Task 1 - Data Collection and Survey
 1.1 Data Collection and Review- Consultant shall collect and review relevant items to
 be utilized for the hydrologic and hydraulic modeling effort. Data includes, but is
 not limited to:

 • Most recent LiDAR terrain information
 • Stormwater GIS Inventory
 • Stormwater Drainage Basins (provided by City)
 • Existing FEMA Base Level Engineering Study

 1.2 Limited Field Survey- Consultant shall determine the locations needed for field
 survey based on the data review. Anticipated required field survey includes, but
 is not limited to:
 • Roadway crossings (approx. 9 locations) – Measurements to verify
 dimensions and invert elevations
 • Open Channel cross sections of Drain 2 (approx. 10 locations)

Task 2 - Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modeling

1) Hydrologic Modeling- Hydrologic analysis will be performed to generate flows and
 hydrographs for the 1D/2D Unsteady hydraulic model. City provided drainage areas will be
 subdivided to ensure adequate computational points and capture effects of significant
 hydrologic features such as culverts, major outfalls, railroad crossings, and other features.
 SCS Curve Number methodology will be used for infiltration and runoff parameters. NOAA
 Atlas 14 will be used for precipitation estimates for design storms. The hydrologic model will
 be executed for a range of storm events including the 5-, 10-, 25-, 50-, and 100-year storms.
 Results of the model will be reviewed/compared to existing models, if available.

2) Hydraulic Modeling- A 1D/2D, unsteady hydraulic model will be developed to estimate water
 surface elevations (WSEL) and flooding inundation for the simulated storm events.
 Channels and culvert crossings will be modeled in 1D and connected to the 2D surface.

 The model will reflect the most current terrain data and land use data for model parameters,
 including roughness values, obstructions, and ineffective flow areas. Culverts and storm
 pipes will be added to the model as needed based on GIS information and field survey data.
 The hydraulic model will be executed for a range of storm events including the 5-, 10-, 25-,
 50-, and 100-year storms and compared to existing models, if available.

3) Identify improvement projects to improve drainage and reduce flooding within the basin. The
 proposed improvements may consist of detention and/or conveyance improvements
 including ditch widening, ditch cleanout, and culvert upsizing.

Task 3 – Design Layouts and Estimates

 improvement alternatives.
5) Final schematic drawings and construction budget cost estimates completed based on
 selected alternative(s).

GENERAL DESCRIPTION – Candlewood Additional Study
The Engineer will provide all professional services necessary to perform additional flood hazard
study of the Candlewood neighborhood. The study includes updating the existing conditions and
analyzing additional alternatives. The study is more particularly defined by Tasks 1 and 2
(Existing Conditions Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modeling & Alternatives Analysis), and final
deliverable includes a report with recommendations for future capital improvements.

Task 4 - Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modeling

1) Existing Conditions Modeling- Update the previously developed 2-D HEC-RAS model to
 include the Wolfsbridge development. Incorporate the change in landuse and the detention
 pond within the development. The City will provide the development plans and proposed
 digital surface, if available.

2) Identify any potential downstream impacts to homes, roads, and drainage infrastructure from
 the Wolfsbridge development. Compare pre-development flows and water surface
 elevations to post-development.

Task 5 – Alternatives Analysis

Proposed conditions modeling will be performed for additional alternatives. Preliminary cost and
feasibility will be performed for each alternative. The additional alternatives are outlined below:

3) Alternative 1 – North Channel. Extend proposed channel improvements from Lassiter Lane
 to Kerr Station Road.
4) Alternative 2 – Conveyance Improvements. Analyze neighborhood wide channel
 improvements and culvert capacity improvements. Determine the feasible level of service
 able to be provided through conveyance improvements only.
5) Alternative 3 – Regional detention. Analyze additional areas where regional detention could
 be located and determine potential benefits.
6) Alternative 4 – Buyouts. Determine feasibility and cost-effectiveness of buyouts in
 comparison to flood control projects. Identify if any locations would potentially qualify for
 funding.
